sections.heading: Why an Expired Registration Ticket in El Paso Is Worth Fighting
paragraphs: Expired registration is the citation El Paso officers write most often as an add-on. You get pulled over on Montana Avenue or Mesa Street for something else, the officer runs the plate, and the sticker that lapsed two months ago becomes a second ticket. In Texas, paying is a guilty plea: the conviction goes on your record, and with court costs set by the court you pay for a sticker you were going to renew anyway.

The frustrating part is that the law is built to let you out of this ticket. Texas Transportation Code 502.407 generally allows a judge to dismiss an expired-registration charge when the driver shows the vehicle was registered within 20 working days of the citation and pays an administrative fee set by the court. Courts in El Paso County apply it routinely — but only if someone asks, with the right proof. That is the job our office does for you.
If the registration ticket came with a no-insurance or speeding citation from the same stop, we handle all of them together, and each extra citation is a discounted add-on on the checkout page.

sections.heading: The 2025 Inspection Change — and Why El Paso Is Different
paragraphs: For years Texas ran the "Two Steps, One Sticker" program: you passed a safety inspection first, then renewed your registration, and a single windshield sticker covered both. That is why so many older tickets read "expired inspection" or "no inspection certificate."

Starting in 2025, Texas ended the annual safety inspection requirement for most non-commercial vehicles and replaced it with an inspection program replacement fee collected with registration. But El Paso County is one of the Texas counties with a vehicle emissions program, so most gasoline cars and pickups registered here still need a passing emissions inspection before the registration can be renewed. The safety check went away; the emissions step did not.

This matters for your ticket. An "expired inspection" citation on a personal vehicle may rest on a requirement that has changed, and the details of what was required on the citation date are something we review case by case. If you were cited for expired registration, the fix has not changed: pass emissions if your vehicle needs it, renew, bring the receipt, and let us ask the court for the statutory dismissal. Our ticket dismissal page explains what a dismissal means for your record.

sections.heading: Four Ways a Registration Ticket Gets Resolved
paragraphs: When you hire us online or call 915-503-1600, we file a notice of appearance with the court promptly, which stops any failure-to-appear problem and routes the court's notices to our office. Then we tell you exactly what to do on your end: renew the registration (online, at an El Paso County Tax Office location, or at a participating grocery store) and send us a photo of the receipt and the new sticker.

With that proof in hand, we present the case to the prosecutor and ask for the dismissal the statute allows. Where the 20-working-day window has already passed, we still have options: deferred disposition under Code of Criminal Procedure art. 45.051, which ends in a dismissal with no conviction, or a negotiated outcome that keeps the violation off your record. Our goal is to pursue the best available outcome based on the citation, driving record, court and circumstances.

sections.heading: Fort Bliss, Out-of-State and Mexican Plates
paragraphs: El Paso's registration tickets have a local twist. Thousands of soldiers at Fort Bliss drive cars registered in Georgia, Kentucky or wherever they last served, and Texas generally does not require active-duty military to switch to Texas registration as long as the home-state registration is valid. An officer who sees an unfamiliar sticker may still write the ticket. If your out-of-state registration was current, we bring the proof and your military orders to the prosecutor and ask for a dismissal.

Civilians who move here for work face a different rule: Texas generally expects new residents to register within 30 days, and the first "welcome to Texas" ticket often arrives before the paperwork is done. Chihuahua plates on a car driven by an El Paso resident raise their own questions about where the vehicle is actually kept. The answer depends on the documents you can show. Not sure where your ticket was filed, or whether a missed date turned into a warrant? Use the free ticket and warrant lookup.

sections.heading: Which El Paso Court Has Your Registration Ticket
paragraphs: El Paso Police citations go to El Paso Municipal Court on Overland Avenue, where our flat fee is $59. Tickets from the Sheriff's Office, a DPS trooper on I-10 or a constable go to a Justice of the Peace precinct. Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint and Anthony each run their own municipal courts; our fee in those courts is $69. The approach is the same everywhere: prove the fix, ask for the dismissal, and keep you out of the courtroom.

Check the appearance date printed on your citation, don't pay it, and don't miss it. faqs.q: Can an expired registration ticket be dismissed in El Paso?
faqs.a: Generally, yes. Texas Transportation Code 502.407 lets the court dismiss the charge when you register the vehicle within 20 working days of the citation and pay an administrative fee set by the court. If you missed that window, we ask for deferred disposition or another outcome that avoids a conviction.

faqs.q: Do I still need a vehicle inspection in El Paso?
faqs.a: The annual safety inspection ended in 2025 for most non-commercial vehicles, but El Paso County has a vehicle emissions program, so most gasoline cars and pickups registered here still need a passing emissions inspection before renewal. Commercial vehicles have separate rules.

faqs.q: What happens if I just pay the registration ticket?
faqs.a: Paying is a guilty plea. The conviction goes on your record, you pay the fine plus court costs, and you still have to renew the registration. Hiring us costs $59–$69 and is aimed at ending the case with no conviction at all.

faqs.q: I'm stationed at Fort Bliss with out-of-state plates. Was the ticket valid?
faqs.a: Often not. Active-duty service members may generally keep valid home-state registration while stationed in Texas. If your registration was current, we present the proof and your orders to the prosecutor and ask for a dismissal.

faqs.q: Will I have to go to court?
faqs.a: Generally not. We file an appearance, gather your proof of registration and handle the pretrial docket for you. The only time you might appear is at a trial, which is uncommon for this type of ticket and something we would discuss with you first.

faqs.q: My registration ticket came with a no-insurance ticket. Can you handle both?
faqs.a: Yes. Multiple citations from the same stop are handled together, with each additional citation at a discounted add-on rate. See our no insurance ticket page for how we approach the insurance charge.
